title: Final debrief: the 'fair' spread model trained on 2012–2019
rubric: Identifies the flaw: the 'fair' spread of ≈ 8 % comes from pooling two regimes (≈ 16 % before 2016, ≈ 6 % after); it describes neither, so the current 6 % is not 'too narrow'.

Brings the evidence: sub-period means and pass-through (4.1), Chow on returns F ≈ 107 at 2016-01-01 with clean placebos (4.2), full-sample Engle-Granger p ≈ 0.28 vs strong cointegration within each regime.
Explains the mechanism behind the break: the end of the export ban opened the arbitrage route, structurally reducing the discount and tightening the daily link.
States what the current-regime model says instead: equilibrium discount ≈ 6 %, adjustment ≈ 11 % per day (half-life ≈ 6 days), so today's spread is close to equilibrium — no trade signal.
Describes the right procedure: economic reasoning for possible breaks, estimate within the current regime, test the stability with a known-date test on stationary variables, re-test regularly.
Acknowledges limits: break dates are rarely sharp; a new regime may be starting; tests have limited power; the analysis is descriptive, not a backtested strategy.
Delivered as a conclusion-first, evidence-backed answer a PM can act on.
